title.zh: 卷252 列傳三十九 甘文焜 范承谟 马雄镇 傅宏烈
title.en: Volume 252 Biographies 39: Gan Wenkun, Fan Chengmo, Ma Xiongzhen, Fu Honglie
title.raw: 卷252 列傳三十九 甘文焜 范承谟 马雄镇 傅宏烈

sentences.zh: 列傳三十九

translations.literal: Biographies 39
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 39

sentences.zh: =甘文焜=甘文焜，字炳如，漢軍正藍旗人，其先自豐城徙瀋陽。

translations.literal: Gan Wenkun. Gan Wenkun, styled Bingru, was a member of the Han military Plain Blue Banner; his forebears had moved from Fengcheng to Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Wenkun, styled Bingru, belonged to the Han military Plain Blue Banner; his family had earlier moved from Fengcheng to Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 父應魁，從入關，官至石匣副將。

translations.literal: His father Yingkui followed the entry into China proper and rose to deputy commander at Shixia.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yingkui followed the armies south at the conquest and eventually became deputy commander at Shixia.

sentences.zh: 文焜善騎射，喜讀書，尤慕古忠孝事。

translations.literal: Wenkun excelled at mounted archery, loved reading, and especially admired ancient stories of loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun was skilled in horsemanship and archery, devoted to books, and above all drawn to ancient tales of loyalty and filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 以官學生授兵部筆帖式，累遷禮部啟心郎，屢奉使稱旨。

translations.literal: As a student of the Imperial Academy he was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of War, was promoted through posts to Qixin Lang in the Ministry of Rites, and on repeated missions won imperial praise.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as an academy student, he became a clerk in the Ministry of War, rose to Qixin Lang in the Ministry of Rites, and on successive missions so pleased the throne that he won repeated commendation.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，授大理寺少卿，遷順天府府尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kangxi reign he was made vice-president of the Court of Judicial Review and then transferred to governor of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangxi reign he was appointed vice-president of the Court of Judicial Review and then promoted to governor of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 崇文門榷稅不平，疏劾之。

translations.literal: The transit tax at Chongwen Gate was unjust; he memorialized to impeach it.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the levies at Chongwen Gate unfair, he submitted a memorial of impeachment.

sentences.zh: 廷議令兼攝，文焜曰：「言之而居之，是利之也。

translations.literal: The court deliberated having him hold the post concurrently; Wenkun said: "To speak against it and then occupy it is to profit from it.
translations.idiomatic: When the court proposed that he take the post himself, Wenkun said, "To denounce an abuse and then hold the office is to profit from it.

sentences.zh: 」固辭。

translations.literal: " He firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: " He refused firmly.

sentences.zh: 六年，授直隸巡撫，奏复巡歷舊制。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed governor of Zhili and memorialized to restore the old system of inspection tours.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became governor of Zhili and memorialized to revive the former practice of touring the province.

sentences.zh: 單車按部，適保定、真定所屬諸縣患水災，疏請蠲歲賦。

translations.literal: He made his rounds with a single cart; counties under Baoding and Zhending had suffered flood, and he memorialized to remit the year's land tax.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling alone with a single cart on his inspection, he found flood damage in counties under Baoding and Zhending and memorialized to waive the year's land tax.

sentences.zh: 總督白秉真以賑費浩繁，請聽官民輸銀米。

translations.literal: Governor-General Bai Bingzhen, citing vast relief costs, asked that officials and people be allowed to contribute silver and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Bai Bingzhen, citing the enormous cost of relief, proposed that officials and commoners be permitted to donate silver and grain.

sentences.zh: 文焜斥廉俸以助。

translations.literal: Wenkun contributed his integrity stipend to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun drew on his own integrity stipend to help.

sentences.zh: 議敘，加工部侍郎。

translations.literal: On review of merit he was given the additional rank of vice-president of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When his service was reviewed, he received the additional rank of vice-president of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷雲貴總督，駐貴陽。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou, stationed at Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou, with his headquarters at Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 時吳三桂鎮雲南，欲藉邊釁固兵權，詭報土番康東入寇，紿文焜移師，又陰嗾凱里諸苗乘其後。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Sangui held Yunnan and wished to use border troubles to secure military power; he falsely reported that the aboriginal tribe Kangdong had invaded, tricked Wenkun into moving troops, and secretly incited the Miao of Kaili to strike from behind.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui then held Yunnan and sought to use border alarms to keep his armies under his hand; he fabricated a report that the Kangdong tribesmen had raided, lured Wenkun into shifting his forces, and secretly set the Kaili Miao to attack his rear.

sentences.zh: 文焜策康東無能為，凱里近肘腋，不制將滋蔓，先督兵搗其巢，斬苗酋阿戎。

translations.literal: Wenkun judged Kangdong could do little harm, but that Kaili, close at his side, would spread if unchecked; he first led troops to destroy their nest and beheaded the Miao chieftain Arong.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun reckoned Kangdong no serious threat, but that Kaili lay too near his flank and would grow worse if left alone; he marched first against their stronghold and beheaded the Miao chief Arong.

sentences.zh: 既平，約雲南會剿康東。

translations.literal: Once pacified, he arranged a joint campaign with Yunnan against Kangdong.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory he arranged with Yunnan for a joint expedition against Kangdong.

sentences.zh: 三桂慮詐洩，謂康東已遠遁，繇是益憚之。

translations.literal: Sangui feared his deceit would leak out and said Kangdong had fled far away; from this he feared Wenkun all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui, afraid his fraud would be exposed, claimed Kangdong had already fled into the distance—and from that point feared Wenkun still more.

sentences.zh: 文焜巡歷雲、貴各府州皆遍。

translations.literal: Wenkun toured every prefecture and department in Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun made inspection tours through every prefecture and department in Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，遭母憂，上命在任守制。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was bereaved of his mother; the throne ordered him to observe mourning while remaining in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year his mother died; the emperor ordered him to observe mourning without leaving his post.

sentences.zh: 文焜又遣兵擊殺臻剖苗酋阿福。

translations.literal: Wenkun again sent troops to attack and kill Afu, chieftain of the Zhenpou Miao.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun again sent troops against the Zhenpou Miao and killed their chief Afu.

sentences.zh: 疏乞歸葬，許給假治喪。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to return home for burial; leave to conduct the funeral was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to go home for the burial, and was granted leave to perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 三桂請以雲南巡撫兼督篆，令督標兵悉詣雲南受節度，而以利啗之，冀為己用。

translations.literal: Sangui requested that he concurrently hold the governorship of Yunnan and the commander's seal, that all troops under the governor-general's banner go to Yunnan to accept his command, and tried to win him with profit, hoping to use him.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui asked that Wenkun also hold the Yunnan governorship and commander's seal, that all troops of the governor-general's banner be sent to Yunnan under his orders, and tempted him with rewards, hoping to win him over.

sentences.zh: 十二年，文焜還本官，適撤籓議起。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Wenkun returned to his original post, just as discussion of abolishing the feudatories arose.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Wenkun resumed his former office just as the court began debating the abolition of the feudatories.

sentences.zh: 三桂反，殺巡撫硃國治，遣其黨偪貴陽。

translations.literal: Sangui rebelled, killed Governor Zhu Guozhi, and sent his partisans to press Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui rose in rebellion, killed the Yunnan governor Zhu Guozhi, and sent his followers to threaten Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 文焜聞變，使族弟文炯齎奏入告，牒貴州提督李本深率兵扼盤江。

translations.literal: On hearing the revolt Wenkun sent his clansman Wen Jiong bearing a memorial to report to the capital and dispatched orders to Guizhou Provincial Commander Li Benshen to lead troops and hold Pan River.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard of the uprising, Wenkun sent his kinsman Wen Jiong with a memorial to the capital and ordered Guizhou commander Li Benshen to take troops and block the Pan River crossing.

sentences.zh: 本深已懷貳，先以書覘文焜意。

translations.literal: Benshen already harbored disloyalty and first sent a letter to probe Wenkun's intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Li Benshen was already of two minds and first wrote to sound Wenkun out.

sentences.zh: 文焜手書報之，期效張巡、南霽雲誓死守，而本深不之顧。

translations.literal: Wenkun replied in his own hand, pledging to emulate Zhang Xun and Nan Jiyun in swearing to die defending the post, but Benshen paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun answered in his own hand, vowing to follow Zhang Xun and Nan Jiyun in holding the place to the death—but Benshen ignored him.

sentences.zh: 本標兵已受三桂餌，紛潰弗聽調。

translations.literal: Benshen's banner troops had already taken Sangui's bribes and scattered in disorder, refusing orders.
translations.idiomatic: Li's own banner troops had already been bought by Sangui; they broke ranks and would not obey.

sentences.zh: 文焜度貴陽不可守，令妾盛率婦女七人自經死，獨攜第四子國城赴鎮遠，思召湖北兵扼險隘，使賊不北出。

translations.literal: Wenkun judged Guiyang could not be held; he ordered his concubine Sheng to lead seven women in hanging themselves, and went alone with his fourth son Guocheng to Zhenyuan, planning to summon Hubei troops to hold the passes and keep the rebels from marching north.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Guiyang indefensible, Wenkun had his concubine Sheng lead seven women of the household to hang themselves, then set out alone with his fourth son Guocheng for Zhenyuan, hoping to rally Hubei troops at the mountain passes and keep the rebels from breaking north.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙申朔，癸卯至鎮遠，守將江義已受偽命，拒弗納。

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month, day bingshen, on day guimao he reached Zhenyuan; the defending commander Jiang Yi had already accepted a rebel commission and refused him entry.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the twelfth month (day bingshen) he set out; on day guimao he reached Zhenyuan, where the garrison commander Jiang Yi, having already taken orders from the rebels, shut him out.

sentences.zh: 文焜渡河至吉祥寺，義遣兵圍之。

translations.literal: Wenkun crossed the river to Jixiang Temple; Yi sent troops to surround him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun crossed the river to Jixiang Temple, and Jiang Yi sent troops to surround him.

sentences.zh: 文焜望闕再拜，拔佩刀將自殺，國城大呼請先死，奪其刀以刎而還之，屍乃踣，血濺文焜衣。

translations.literal: Wenkun bowed toward the palace twice, drew his sword to kill himself; Guocheng cried out asking to die first, seized the blade, cut his own throat and returned the sword; the body fell, blood splashing Wenkun's robe.
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun bowed twice toward the imperial court, drew his sword to take his own life; Guocheng shouted that he should die first, wrested away the blade, cut his own throat, and handed the sword back—then collapsed, his blood spattering Wenkun's robes.

sentences.zh: 文焜曰：「是兒勇過我！

translations.literal: Wenkun said: "This boy is braver than I!
translations.idiomatic: Wenkun said, "This child is braver than I!

sentences.zh: 」遂自殺，年四十有二。

translations.literal: " He then killed himself, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he took his own life. He was forty-two.

sentences.zh: 從者筆帖式和善雅圖殉。

translations.literal: His attendant clerk Heshanyatu died with him.
translations.idiomatic: His clerk Heshanyatu died at his side.

sentences.zh: 亂平，貴州巡撫楊雍建以文焜治績及死事狀上聞，予優恤。

translations.literal: When the rebellion was pacified, Guizhou Governor Yang Yongjian reported Wenkun's administrative achievements and manner of death to the throne, and exceptional condolence gifts were granted.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, Guizhou governor Yang Yongjian memorialized Wenkun's record in office and the circumstances of his death, and the court granted him exceptional posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 遣其長子宣化同知國均迎喪還京師，使內大臣佟國維迎奠盧溝橋，贈兵部尚書，諡忠果。

translations.literal: His eldest son Guojun, sub-prefect of Xuanhua, was sent to bring the coffin back to the capital; Inner Minister Tong Guowei was ordered to receive and offer sacrifice at Lugou Bridge; he was posthumously made minister of war with the posthumous title Zhongguo.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Guojun, sub-prefect of Xuanhua, was sent to escort the coffin to Beijing; Inner Minister Tong Guowei received the bier and offered sacrifice at Lugou Bridge; Wenkun was posthumously made Minister of War and given the posthumous name Zhongguo, "Loyal and Resolute."

sentences.zh: 建祠貴陽，上賜「勁節」二字顏其額。

translations.literal: A shrine was built at Guiyang; the throne bestowed the two characters "Steadfast Integrity" to inscribe its tablet.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine was raised at Guiyang, and the emperor inscribed its plaque with the two characters "Steadfast Integrity."

sentences.zh: 子七，國璧尤知名。

translations.literal: He had seven sons; Guobi was especially well known.
translations.idiomatic: He left seven sons, of whom Guobi became especially renowned.

sentences.zh: 國璧，字東屏，以任子授陝州知州，改蘇州同知，擢山西平陽、浙江寧波知府，名循吏。

translations.literal: Guobi, styled Dongping, was appointed prefect of Shaanzhou by hereditary privilege, transferred to sub-prefect of Suzhou, promoted to prefect of Pingyang in Shanxi and Ningbo in Zhejiang, and was famed as an exemplary local official.
translations.idiomatic: Guobi, styled Dongping, entered office as prefect of Shaanzhou through his father's rank, later served as sub-prefect of Suzhou, and rose to govern Pingyang in Shanxi and Ningbo in Zhejiang, winning a reputation as a model magistrate.

sentences.zh: 聖祖南巡，幸杭州，御書硃子詩及「永貞」額以賜。

translations.literal: On the Sacred Ancestor's southern tour he visited Hangzhou and bestowed in his own hand a poem in Zhu Xi's style and a plaque reading "Ever Chaste."
translations.idiomatic: When the Kangxi Emperor toured the south and visited Hangzhou, he wrote out a poem in the manner of Zhu Xi and bestowed a plaque bearing the words "Ever Chaste."

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「汝父盡節，朕未嘗忘，此為汝母書也。

translations.literal: He instructed him: "Your father died fulfilling his duty; I have not forgotten—this inscription is for your mother.
translations.idiomatic: He told him, "Your father died in loyal service, and I have not forgotten; I write this for your mother.

sentences.zh: 」累遷雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: " He was promoted through posts to governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: " He was eventually promoted to governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 坐事罷。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed after an offense.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，起為正黃旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng reign he was recalled as commander of the Han military Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng he was recalled to command the Han military Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，授綏遠城右翼副都統。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong he was made deputy lieutenant-general of the right wing at Suiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong year three he was appointed deputy lieutenant-general of the right wing at Suiyuan.

sentences.zh: 复罷。

translations.literal: He was again dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed again.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he died.

sentences.zh: =范承謨=范承謨，字覲公，漢軍鑲黃旗人，文程次子。

translations.literal: Fan Chengmo. Fan Chengmo, styled Jingong, was a member of the Han military Bordered Yellow Banner and the second son of Fan Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chengmo, styled Jingong, belonged to the Han military Bordered Yellow Banner and was the second son of Fan Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 順治九年進士，選庶吉士，授弘文院編修。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and appointed compiler in the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Shunzhi year nine, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was made a compiler in the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 累遷秘書院學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted through posts to academician of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through posts to academician of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 康熙七年，授浙江巡撫。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kangxi he was appointed governor of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year seven he became governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 時去開國未久，民流亡未復業，浙東寧波、金華等六府荒田尤多。

translations.literal: The founding was not long past; the people had fled and not returned to their fields, and in eastern Zhejiang the six prefectures of Ningbo, Jinhua, and others had especially much wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: Not many years had passed since the founding; refugees had not yet returned to their farms, and in eastern Zhejiang the six prefectures including Ningbo and Jinhua held especially large tracts of abandoned land.

sentences.zh: 總督趙廷臣請除賦額，上命承謨履勘。

translations.literal: Governor-General Zhao Tingchen asked to reduce the tax quota; the throne ordered Chengmo to conduct an on-site survey.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Zhao Tingchen proposed cutting the tax assessments, and the emperor ordered Chengmo to inspect the land in person.

sentences.zh: 承謨遍歷諸府，請免荒田及水沖田地賦凡三十一萬五千五百馀畝。

translations.literal: Chengmo toured every prefecture and asked exemption of tax on wasteland and land washed away by water, totaling more than 315,500 mu.
translations.idiomatic: Chengmo traveled through every prefecture and memorialized to exempt tax on wasteland and flood-damaged fields—more than 315,500 mu in all.

sentences.zh: 杭州、嘉興、湖州、紹興四府被水，民飢，承謨出布政使庫銀八萬，糴米湖廣平糶，最貧者得附老弱例，肩鹽給朝夕，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: The four prefectures of Hangzhou, Jiaxing, Huzhou, and Shaoxing suffered flood; the people starved; Chengmo drew eighty thousand taels from the provincial treasurer's vault, bought grain in Huguang and sold it at fair price; the poorest were allowed under the aged-and-infirm rule to carry salt on the shoulder for daily sustenance, and very many were kept alive.
translations.idiomatic: When flood struck Hangzhou, Jiaxing, Huzhou, and Shaoxing and the people went hungry, Chengmo took eighty thousand taels from the provincial treasury, purchased grain in Huguang, and sold it at a fair price; the poorest were allowed, under the rule for the aged and helpless, to earn their meals by peddling salt, and a great multitude were saved from starvation.

sentences.zh: 並疏請「漕米改折，石銀一兩。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Let tribute grain be commuted, one tael of silver per shi.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "Let grain tribute be commuted to silver at one tael per shi.

sentences.zh: 明年麥熟，補徵白糧，以三年帶徵。

translations.literal: Next year when the wheat ripens, collect the white grain tax in arrears, to be levied over three years.
translations.idiomatic: When the wheat ripens next year, the white-grain levy may be made up, spread over three years.

sentences.zh: 災重者如例蠲免」。

translations.literal: Where disaster is severe, remit according to precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Where the damage is worst, grant remissions as usual."

sentences.zh: 得旨允行。

translations.literal: Imperial approval was granted and the measures carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved, and the plan was put into effect.

sentences.zh: 十年，以疾請解職，召還。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, citing illness he asked to resign; he was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he asked to resign on grounds of illness and was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 總督劉兆麒、提督塞白理疏言浙民請留承謨一百五十馀牒，給事中姜希轍、柯聳，御史何元英等亦言：「承謨受事三載，愛民如子，不通請謁饋遺。

translations.literal: Governor-General Liu Zhaoqi and Provincial Commander Saibaili memorialized that the people of Zhejiang had submitted more than 150 petitions asking Chengmo to remain; the supervising secretaries Jiang Xizhe and Ke Song and the censor He Yuanying also said: "Chengmo has held office three years, loves the people as his children, and will have nothing to do with lobbying or gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Liu Zhaoqi and commander Saibaili reported that Zhejiang commoners had sent more than 150 petitions begging Chengmo to stay; supervising secretaries Jiang Xizhe and Ke Song and censor He Yuanying wrote: "In three years in office Chengmo has treated the people like his own children and refused every sort of solicitation and gift.

sentences.zh: 劾罷貪墨，廉治巨猾，剔除加耗、陋規、私派諸弊。

translations.literal: He impeached and removed the corrupt, punished great rascals with integrity, and eliminated the abuses of surcharges, petty exactions, and unauthorized levies.
translations.idiomatic: He has impeached corrupt officials, punished powerful wrongdoers, and rooted out surcharges, petty exactions, and illegal levies.

sentences.zh: 浙民愛戴，深於飢渴。

translations.literal: The people of Zhejiang love and honor him as deeply as hunger and thirst.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Zhejiang cherish him as one longs for food and drink in want.

sentences.zh: 」上命承謨留任。

translations.literal: " The throne ordered Chengmo to remain in office.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered Chengmo to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 十一年，承謨复疏言湖、嘉兩府白糧加耗，多寡不一，請每石加四斗五升為限；

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Chengmo again memorialized that surcharges on white grain in the prefectures of Huzhou and Jiaxing varied in amount and asked that a limit of four dou and five sheng per shi be set;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Chengmo memorialized again that surcharges on white grain in Huzhou and Jiaxing varied wildly and asked that they be capped at four dou and five sheng per shi;

sentences.zh: 又奏蠲溫、台二衛康熙九年以前逋賦及石門、平陽未完輕齎月糧：皆下戶部議行。

translations.literal: he also memorialized to remit arrears before Kangxi year nine for the two guards of Wenzhou and Taizhou and unpaid light-transport monthly grain for Shimen and Pingyang: all were referred to the Ministry of Revenue for deliberation and execution.
translations.idiomatic: he also asked remission of tax arrears before Kangxi year nine for the Wenzhou and Taizhou guards and of unpaid light-transport grain for Shimen and Pingyang—all referred to the Ministry of Revenue for approval.

sentences.zh: 十月，擢福建總督，疏辭未允，請入覲。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian; his memorial declining was not accepted, and he asked to come to audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was made governor-general of Fujian; when he tried to decline, the court refused, and he asked leave to appear before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 十二年七月，至京師，入對。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twelfth year he reached the capital and had audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twelfth year he reached Beijing and was received in audience.

sentences.zh: 承謨疾未癒，命御醫診視，賜藥餌。

translations.literal: Chengmo's illness had not healed; the throne ordered imperial physicians to examine him and bestowed medicines.
translations.idiomatic: Chengmo was still ill; the emperor sent court physicians to treat him and gave him medicine.

sentences.zh: 疾稍差，趣赴官，賜冠服、鞍馬。

translations.literal: When his illness improved slightly he was urged to take up his post and was given court dress and saddle horse.
translations.idiomatic: When he improved a little he was pressed to take up his post and was given court robes and a saddle horse.

sentences.zh: 福建總督初駐漳州，至是以將撤籓，命移駐福州。

translations.literal: The Fujian governor-general had first been stationed at Zhangzhou; now, because the feudatories were to be abolished, he was ordered to move headquarters to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Fujian governor-general had first been posted at Zhangzhou; with the feudatories about to be abolished, he was ordered to move his headquarters to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂反，承謨察精忠有異志，時方議裁兵，承謨疏請緩行。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Chengmo perceived that Jingzhong harbored disloyal intent; troops were then under discussion for reduction, and Chengmo memorialized asking delay.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Chengmo saw that Geng Jingzhong was disloyal at heart; the court was then debating troop reductions, and Chengmo memorialized to proceed slowly.

sentences.zh: 又報巡歷邊海，欲置身外郡，便徵調防禦。

translations.literal: He also reported that he would tour the coastal border, wishing to place himself in an outer prefecture to facilitate mobilization for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that he would tour the coast, planning to station himself in an outlying prefecture where he could more easily call up troops for defense.

sentences.zh: 事未行而精忠叛，陽言海寇至，約承謨計事。

translations.literal: Before this could be carried out Jingzhong rebelled, falsely claiming sea bandits had arrived, and invited Chengmo to consult on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could act, Geng Jingzhong rose in rebellion, pretended that pirates had appeared, and summoned Chengmo to discuss the matter.

sentences.zh: 巡撫劉秉政附精忠，趣同行。

translations.literal: Governor Liu Bingzheng sided with Jingzhong and urged him to go together.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Liu Bingzheng had thrown in with Geng Jingzhong and pressed Chengmo to go with them.

sentences.zh: 承謨知有變，左右請擐甲從，承謨曰：「眾寡不敵，備無益也。

translations.literal: Chengmo knew trouble had come; his attendants asked him to don armor and go armed; Chengmo said: "We are too few to match them; preparations would do no good.
translations.idiomatic: Chengmo knew something was wrong; his attendants urged him to go in armor, but he said, "We are outnumbered; armor would do no good.

sentences.zh: 」遂往。

translations.literal: " He went.
translations.idiomatic: " He went anyway.

sentences.zh: 精忠之徒露刃相脅，承謨挺身前，罵不絕口。

translations.literal: Jingzhong's followers bared blades to threaten him; Chengmo stepped forward and cursed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jingzhong's men drew their swords to threaten him; Chengmo stepped forward and rained curses on them.

sentences.zh: 精忠拘之土室，加以桎梏，絕粒十日，不得死。

translations.literal: Jingzhong confined him in an earthen cell, put him in fetters, and starved him ten days without bringing death.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jingzhong shut him in a cell of beaten earth, put him in irons, and starved him for ten days, yet he would not die.

sentences.zh: 精忠遣秉政說降，承謨奮足蹴之僕，叱左右掖之出，曰：「賊就僇當不遠，我先褫其魄！

translations.literal: Jingzhong sent Bingzheng to urge surrender; Chengmo kicked the messenger down with his foot, shouted for attendants to drag him out, and said: "The rebels' execution is not far off—I will first strip them of their courage!
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jingzhong sent Bingzheng to win him over; Chengmo kicked the envoy to the ground and ordered his men to drag him out, crying, "The rebels' day of execution is near—I will break their spirit first!

sentences.zh: 」為賊困逾二年，日冠賜冠，衣辭母時衣，遇朔望，奉時憲書一帙懸之，北鄉再拜。

translations.literal: " Held captive by the rebels more than two years, daily he wore the court cap bestowed on him and the robe he had worn when taking leave of his mother; on the first and fifteenth of the month he hung up a volume of the calendar and bowed twice toward the north.
translations.idiomatic: " For more than two years in rebel hands he daily wore the court cap the emperor had given him and the robe he had worn when bidding his mother farewell; on the first and fifteenth of each month he hung up the official calendar and bowed twice toward the north.

sentences.zh: 所居室迫隘，號曰蒙谷。

translations.literal: The room where he lived was cramped; he called it the Dark Valley.
translations.idiomatic: His quarters were cramped, and he called them the Dark Valley.

sentences.zh: 為詩文，以桴炭畫壁上。

translations.literal: He composed poetry and prose, writing them on the wall with torch charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote poems and essays on the walls in charcoal from a pine torch.

sentences.zh: 時有部曲張福建者，手刃奪門入，連斬數賊，力竭死。

translations.literal: At the time a soldier under his command named Zhang Fujian, blade in hand, forced the gate and entered, cut down several rebels in succession, and died when his strength was spent.
translations.idiomatic: One of his soldiers, Zhang Fujian, fought his way through the gate with a drawn sword, killed several rebels in succession, and fell when his strength gave out.

sentences.zh: 蒙古人嘛尼為偽散騎郎，精忠遣守承謨，感承謨忠義，謀令出走。

translations.literal: The Mongol Mani served as a false Gentleman Attendant in the Cavalry; Jingzhong sent him to guard Chengmo; moved by Chengmo's loyalty and righteousness, he plotted to let him escape.
translations.idiomatic: A Mongol named Mani held a false post as Gentleman Attendant in the Cavalry and was set to guard Chengmo; touched by his loyalty, Mani plotted to help him escape.

sentences.zh: 事泄，精忠將磔之，大言曰：「吾寧與忠臣同死，不原與逆賊同生！

translations.literal: The plot leaked; Jingzhong was about to dismember him by quartering; he cried out: "I would rather die with a loyal minister than live with rebel traitors!
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered, Geng Jingzhong was about to have him torn apart; Mani cried, "I would rather die with a loyal minister than live with rebel traitors!

sentences.zh: 十五年，師克仙霞關，精忠將降，冀飾詞免死，懼承謨暴其罪。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the army took Xianxia Pass; Jingzhong was about to surrender and hoped to escape death with fine words, but feared Chengmo would expose his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year imperial forces took Xianxia Pass; Geng Jingzhong was ready to surrender and hoped to talk his way out of execution, but feared Chengmo would expose his crimes.

sentences.zh: 九月己酉朔，甲子夜半，精忠遣黨偪承謨就​​縊。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month, day jiyou, at midnight on day jiazi Jingzhong sent his partisans to force Chengmo to hang himself.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the ninth month (day jiyou), at midnight on day jiazi, Geng Jingzhong sent his men to force Chengmo to hang himself.

sentences.zh: 幕客嵇永仁、王龍光、沈天成，從弟承譜，下至隸卒，同死者五十三人。

translations.literal: His secretaries Ji Yongren, Wang Longguang, and Shen Tiancheng, his cousin Chengpu, down to clerks and runners—fifty-three died with him.
translations.idiomatic: His secretaries Ji Yongren, Wang Longguang, and Shen Tiancheng, his cousin Chengpu, and servants down to runners—fifty-three died with him.

sentences.zh: 語互詳忠義傳。

translations.literal: Their stories are given in detail in the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Their accounts are set out at length in the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 舊役王道隆奉遣他出，還至延平，聞變，自刎死。

translations.literal: His former servant Wang Daolong had been sent on another mission; returning to Yanping and hearing of the revolt, he cut his own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: His former servant Wang Daolong had been sent away on business; when he returned to Yanping and heard what had happened, he killed himself.

sentences.zh: 賊焚承謨屍，棄之野，泰宁騎兵許鼎夜負遺骸藏之。

translations.literal: The rebels burned Chengmo's corpse and cast it in the wilds; the Taining cavalryman Xu Ding carried the remains away by night and hid them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels burned Chengmo's body and threw it in the open country; a Taining cavalryman named Xu Ding carried off the remains by night and hid them.

sentences.zh: 十六年，喪還京師。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the coffin was returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year his coffin was brought back to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 上遣內大臣侍衛迎奠，贈兵部尚書、太子少保，諡忠貞，御書碑文賜其家。

translations.literal: The throne sent an inner minister and guards to receive the bier and offer sacrifice; he was posthumously made minister of war and Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Zhongzhen, and an imperial inscription for his stele was bestowed on his family.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an inner minister and guards to receive the bier and offer sacrifice; Chengmo was posthumously made Minister of War and Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, given the posthumous name Zhongzhen, "Loyal and Constant," and an imperially written epitaph for his family.

sentences.zh: 十九年，精忠伏誅。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Jingzhong was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Geng Jingzhong was put to death.

sentences.zh: 赴市曹日，承謨子時崇臠其肉祭墓。

translations.literal: On the day he was taken to the execution ground, Chengmo's son Shichong carved flesh from his body to offer at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Geng Jingzhong went to the execution ground, Chengmo's son Shichong cut flesh from his body to offer at his father's tomb.

sentences.zh: 福建民請建祠祀之，御書「忠貞炳日」扁於楣。

translations.literal: The people of Fujian requested that a shrine be built to worship him; the emperor personally wrote the plaque "Loyal and Constant, Shining Like the Sun" for the lintel.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fujian petitioned to build a shrine in his honor, and the emperor himself wrote the plaque "Loyal and Constant, Shining Like the Sun" for its lintel.

sentences.zh: 承謨所為畫壁集，上親制序。

translations.literal: For the anthology of wall paintings that Chengmo had made, the emperor personally composed the preface.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally wrote a preface for Chengmo's collection of paintings on walls.

sentences.zh: 時崇，字自牧。

translations.literal: Shichong, styled Zimu.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong, styled Zimu.

sentences.zh: 以難廕出知遼陽州，遷直隸順德知府，有惠政。

translations.literal: Through the privilege granted because his father died for the state, he went out to serve as magistrate of Liaoyang Prefecture, was transferred to prefect of Shunde in Zhili, and had benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: Granted office because his father had died in service to the state, he became magistrate of Liaoyang Prefecture, later prefect of Shunde in Zhili, where he governed with kindness.

sentences.zh: 累遷福建按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Fujian provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to become Fujian provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 陛辭日，上顧謂群臣曰：「此開國名臣孫，殉難忠臣子也！

translations.literal: On the day of his audience to take leave, the emperor turned and said to the assembled ministers: "This is the grandson of a founding dynastic minister, the son of a minister who died for his country!
translations.idiomatic: When he took leave at court, the emperor turned to the ministers and said, "This is the grandson of a founding minister of the dynasty, the son of a loyal servant who gave his life in the national crisis!

sentences.zh: 」四十七年，擢廣東巡撫，兼鹽政。

translations.literal: " In the forty-seventh year he was promoted to governor of Guangdong, with concurrent charge of the salt administration.
translations.idiomatic: " In the forty-seventh year he was promoted to governor of Guangdong, with charge of salt revenues as well.

sentences.zh: 越二年，擢福建浙江總督。

translations.literal: Two years later he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Two years on, he was made governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，入為左都御史。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he entered the capital as censor-in-chief of the left.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year he was recalled to the capital as Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 明年，授兵部尚書。

translations.literal: The following year he was appointed minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 命出塞築莫代察罕廋爾、鄂爾齋圖杲爾台站凡四十有七所。

translations.literal: He was ordered beyond the frontier to build forty-seven relay stations at Modai Chahan Ao'er, E'erzhai Tu Gao'er, and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered beyond the frontier to build forty-seven relay stations at Modai Chahan Ao'er, E'erzhai Tu Gao'er, and other posts.

sentences.zh: 又明年，還朝。

translations.literal: The year after that he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 閩人思其德，附祀承謨祠。

translations.literal: The people of Min recalled his virtue and enshrined him jointly in Chengmo's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fujian remembered his kindness and added him to the worship at Chengmo's shrine.

sentences.zh: =馬雄鎮=馬雄鎮，字錫蕃，漢軍鑲紅旗人，鳴佩子。

translations.literal: Ma Xiongzhen. Ma Xiongzhen, styled Xifan, was a member of the Han military Bordered Red Banner, and a son of Mingpei.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiongzhen, styled Xifan, belonged to the Han military Bordered Red Banner and was a son of Mingpei.

sentences.zh: 以廕補工部副理事官，歷遷左僉都御史、國史院學士。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he entered the Ministry of Works as an assistant supervising secretary, and was promoted in succession to Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief and academician of the State Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he entered the Ministry of Works as an assistant supervising secretary and eventually rose to Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief and academician of the State Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，授山西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi he was appointed governor of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Kangxi reign he was appointed governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 未上，改廣西。

translations.literal: Before taking up the post he was transferred to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post he was transferred to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 時群盜蝟起，構瑤、僮掠梧州、平樂二府，不數月討平之。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose everywhere like hedgehogs; Yao and Zhuang were stirred up to plunder the two prefectures of Wuzhou and Pingle, and within a few months he suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits swarmed like hedgehogs; Yao and Zhuang raiders plundered Wuzhou and Pingle prefectures, but within a few months he had suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 累疏請平鹺價，建學宮，定有司邊俸，省軍糧運費，並罷諸採買累民者，皆得旨允行。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized to stabilize salt prices, build Confucian schools, fix border stipends for local officials, reduce military grain transport costs, and abolish various purchase levies that burdened the people; all received imperial approval and were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized to stabilize salt prices, build Confucian schools, fix border stipends for local officials, cut military grain transport costs, and abolish purchase levies that burdened the people; the throne approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 十二年，吳三桂反。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Wu Sangui rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Wu Sangui rebelled.

sentences.zh: 十三年，孫延齡以廣西叛應之，圍雄鎮廨，脅降。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Sun Yanling rebelled in Guangxi in support, besieged Xiongzhen's yamen, and pressured him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Sun Yanling rebelled in Guangxi in support of Wu Sangui, besieged Xiongzhen's yamen, and tried to force his surrender.

sentences.zh: 時巡撫無標​​兵，雄鎮督家人拒守。

translations.literal: At the time the governor had no marked troops; Xiongzhen led his household retainers in a defensive stand.
translations.idiomatic: The governor had no properly marked troops at hand, so Xiongzhen led his household retainers in a defensive stand.

sentences.zh: 密令守備易友亮赴柳州趣提督馬雄來援，弗應。

translations.literal: He secretly ordered the garrison commander Yi Youliang to go to Liuzhou and urge the grand coordinator Ma Xiong to come to the rescue, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly ordered the garrison commander Yi Youliang to go to Liuzhou and urge Grand Coordinator Ma Xiong to send relief, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 雄鎮自經，為家人救免，以蠟丸馳疏請兵。

translations.literal: Xiongzhen tried to hang himself but was saved by his family; he sent an urgent petition for troops sealed in a wax ball.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongzhen tried to hang himself but was saved by his family, then sent an urgent petition for troops sealed in a wax ball.

sentences.zh: 延齡诇知之，幽雄鎮，置家人別室。

translations.literal: Yanling learned through espionage, confined Xiongzhen, and put his family in separate quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling learned of this through spies, confined Xiongzhen, and kept his family in separate quarters.

sentences.zh: 三桂使招降，雄鎮不為屈。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui sent envoys to persuade him to surrender, but Xiongzhen would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui sent envoys to win him over, but Xiongzhen would not yield.

sentences.zh: 會傅弘烈勸延齡反正，延齡躊躇未決，雄鎮得以間遣長子世濟齎疏詣京師，友亮導之出，客楊啟祥護行，至贛州，江西巡撫董衛國以聞。

translations.literal: When Fu Honglie urged Yanling to return to allegiance and Yanling hesitated without deciding, Xiongzhen was able in the interval to send his eldest son Shiji to the capital with a memorial; Youliang guided him out, the guest Yang Qixiang escorted him on the journey, and when they reached Ganzhou, Jiangxi Governor Dong Weiguo reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Honglie urged Yanling to return to loyalty and Yanling wavered, Xiongzhen seized the opportunity to send his eldest son Shiji to the capital with a memorial; Youliang guided him out, the guest Yang Qixiang escorted him, and when they reached Ganzhou, Jiangxi Governor Dong Weiguo reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上遣使護入京，至，授世濟四品京卿。

translations.literal: The throne sent an escort to bring him safely into the capital; on arrival, Shiji was made a fourth-rank capital official.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an escort to bring him safely to the capital; on arrival, Shiji was made a fourth-rank capital official.

sentences.zh: 居數月，雄鎮又具疏陳粵西可復狀，付長孫國楨，俾與客硃昉鑿垣出。

translations.literal: After several months Xiongzhen prepared another memorial setting out conditions in western Guangdong and how it could be recovered, entrusted it to his eldest grandson Guozhen, and had him break through a wall with the guest Zhu Fang to get out.
translations.idiomatic: After several months Xiongzhen prepared another memorial detailing how western Guangdong could be recovered, entrusted it to his eldest grandson Guozhen, and had him break through a wall with the guest Zhu Fang to escape.

sentences.zh: 既，又遣州人唐守道、唐正發潛負次子世永出，次第詣京師。

translations.literal: After that he secretly sent two men of the prefecture, Tang Shoudao and Tang Zhengfa, to smuggle out his second son Shiyong, who in turn made his way to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Then he secretly sent two local men, Tang Shoudao and Tang Zhengfa, to smuggle out his second son Shiyong, who also made his way to the capital in turn.

sentences.zh: 又為延齡知，係其孥於獄。

translations.literal: Yanling learned of this again and imprisoned his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling discovered this as well and imprisoned his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 雄鎮憤自剄，復為賊所奪，幽之別室。

translations.literal: In anger Xiongzhen cut his own throat, but was seized again by the rebels and confined in a separate room.
translations.idiomatic: In anger Xiongzhen cut his own throat, but the rebels seized him again and held him in a separate room.

sentences.zh: 十六年十月，三桂遣其從孫世琮殺延齡，擁雄鎮至賊壘，迫使降，雄鎮大呼曰：「吾義守封疆，不能寸斬汝以報國，死吾分也！

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixteenth year Wu Sangui sent his grand-nephew Shizong to kill Yanling, dragged Xiongzhen to the rebel camp, and forced him to surrender; Xiongzhen cried out: "I have dutifully guarded the frontier and could not cut you down inch by inch to repay the state—death is my portion!
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the sixteenth year Wu Sangui sent his grand-nephew Shizong to kill Yanling, dragged Xiongzhen to the rebel camp, and tried to force his surrender; Xiongzhen shouted, "I have dutifully guarded the frontier and could not cut you down piece by piece to repay the state—death is my portion!

sentences.zh: 」賊戕其幼子世洪、世泰怵之，罵益厲，賊殺之，時年四十有四。

translations.literal: " The rebels killed his younger sons Shihong and Shitai to frighten him; he cursed all the more fiercely, and the rebels killed him; he was forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels killed his younger sons Shihong and Shitai to frighten him; he cursed all the more fiercely, and the rebels killed him. He was forty-four.

sentences.zh: 從者馬雲皋、唐進寶、諸兆元等九人同時死，妻李，妾顧、劉，女二人，世濟妻董、妾苗，並殉。

translations.literal: Nine followers including Ma Yun'gao, Tang Jinbao, and Zhu Zhaoyuan died with him at the same time; his wife Li, concubines Gu and Liu, two daughters, Shiji's wife Dong and concubine Miao—all perished with him.
translations.idiomatic: Nine followers including Ma Yun'gao, Tang Jinbao, and Zhu Zhaoyuan died with him; his wife Li, concubines Gu and Liu, two daughters, Shiji's wife Dong and concubine Miao—all perished as well.

sentences.zh: 語互詳列女傳。

translations.literal: Their accounts are set out in detail in the Biographies of Exemplary Women.
translations.idiomatic: Their stories are given in detail in the Biographies of Exemplary Women.

sentences.zh: 雄鎮屍暴四十馀日，友亮收其骸骨，藁葬焉。

translations.literal: Xiongzhen's corpse lay exposed for more than forty days; Youliang gathered his bones and gave him a straw burial.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongzhen's body lay exposed for more than forty days before Youliang gathered his bones and gave him a straw burial.

sentences.zh: 雄鎮被縶三年，日著書賦詩。

translations.literal: Held captive for three years, Xiongzhen wrote books and composed poetry every day.
translations.idiomatic: Held captive for three years, Xiongzhen wrote books and composed poetry every day.

sentences.zh: 既死，客孫成、陳文煥乘間脫走，抵蒼梧，以所著擊笏樓遺稿及匯草辨疑歸世濟。

translations.literal: After his death the guests Sun Cheng and Chen Wenhuan escaped at an opportune moment, reached Cangwu, and delivered to Shiji his surviving writings from the Strike-the-Hu Hall together with Collected Drafts and Disputed Points.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the guests Sun Cheng and Chen Wenhuan seized an opportunity to escape, reached Cangwu, and delivered to Shiji his surviving writings from the Strike-the-Hu Hall together with Collected Drafts and Disputed Points.

sentences.zh: 十七年，弘烈以雄鎮死狀入告，命議卹。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Honglie reported Xiongzhen's death to the throne, and an order was issued to deliberate mourning honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Honglie reported Xiongzhen's death to the throne, which ordered mourning honors to be deliberated.

sentences.zh: 擢世濟大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: Shiji was promoted to vice-president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji was promoted to vice-president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 成以舉人授同知，文煥授知縣。

translations.literal: Cheng received a post as sub-prefect through his juren degree, and Wenhuan was made a county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was appointed sub-prefect on the strength of his juren degree, and Wenhuan was made a county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 旋又授友亮、守道、正發、啟祥游擊、守備有差。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Youliang, Shoudao, Zhengfa, and Qixiang were appointed to various posts as brigade commanders and garrison commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Youliang, Shoudao, Zhengfa, and Qixiang were appointed to various posts as brigade commanders and garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 十八年，世濟如廣西迎雄鎮喪至京師，贈太子太傅、兵部尚書，諡文毅。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Shiji went to Guangxi to bring Xiongzhen's coffin to the capital; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent and minister of war, with the posthumous title Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Shiji went to Guangxi to bring Xiongzhen's coffin to the capital; Xiongzhen was posthumously made Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent and Minister of War, with the posthumous name Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 三桂既平，歲正，上宴群臣，特命世濟及陳啟泰子汝器至御座前賜酒。

translations.literal: After Wu Sangui was suppressed, at New Year's the emperor feasted the ministers and specially ordered Shiji and Chen Qitai's son Ruqi to come before the imperial seat to be granted wine.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Sangui was suppressed, at New Year's the emperor feasted the ministers and specially summoned Shiji and Chen Qitai's son Ruqi before the throne to grant them wine.

sentences.zh: 世濟官至遭運總督，世永曆運使；

translations.literal: Shiji rose to Zhaoyun Governor; Shiyong became salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji rose to Zhaoyun Governor; Shiyong became salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 國楨官江南常鎮道，督餉入藏，卒於軍。

translations.literal: Guozhen served as Chang-Zhen Circuit intendant in Jiangnan, supervised grain supplies into Tibet, and died in the field.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen served as Chang-Zhen Circuit intendant in Jiangnan, supervised grain supplies into Tibet, and died on campaign.

sentences.zh: =傅弘烈=傅弘烈，字仲謀，江西進賢人。

translations.literal: Fu Honglie. Fu Honglie, styled Zhongmou, was a native of Jinxian in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Honglie, styled Zhongmou, was a native of Jinxian in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 明末，流寓廣西。

translations.literal: At the end of the Ming he wandered and settled in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Ming dynasty he wandered and settled in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 順治時，以總督王國光薦，授韶州同知，遷甘肅慶陽知府。

translations.literal: During Shunzhi, on the recommendation of Governor-General Wang Guoguang, he was appointed sub-prefect of Shaozhou and later transferred to prefect of Qingyang in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shunzhi reign, on the recommendation of Governor-General Wang Guoguang, he was appointed sub-prefect of Shaozhou and later transferred to prefect of Qingyang in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂蓄逆謀久，康熙七年，弘烈密以告，逮治，坐誣，論斬。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui had long harbored rebellious designs; in the seventh year of Kangxi Honglie secretly reported it, was arrested and tried, was convicted of false accusation, and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui had long harbored rebellious designs; in the seventh year of the Kangxi reign Honglie secretly reported it, was arrested, convicted of false accusation, and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 九年，上特命減死戍梧州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the emperor specially ordered the death sentence reduced to exile at Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the emperor specially ordered the sentence reduced from death to exile at Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 及三桂反，將軍孫延齡、提督馬雄以廣西叛應之。

translations.literal: When Sangui rebelled, General Sun Yanling and Grand Coordinator Ma Xiong rebelled in Guangxi in response.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, General Sun Yanling and Grand Coordinator Ma Xiong rebelled in Guangxi in support.

sentences.zh: 弘烈欲集兵圖恢復，陽受三桂偽職，入思州、泗城、廣南、富川諸土司，歷交阯界，募義軍得五千人，遂移檄討賊，從尚可喜軍規肇慶。

translations.literal: Honglie wished to gather troops and plan recovery; outwardly he accepted a false appointment from Wu Sangui, entered the chieftaincies of Sizhou, Sicheng, Guangnan, and Fuchuan, crossed the border into Annam, raised five thousand volunteer troops, then issued a manifesto to attack the rebels and marched with Shang Kexi's army toward Zhaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie sought to gather troops for recovery; outwardly he accepted a false appointment from Wu Sangui, entered the chieftaincies of Sizhou, Sicheng, Guangnan, and Fuchuan, crossed into Annam, raised five thousand volunteers, issued a manifesto against the rebels, and marched with Shang Kexi's army toward Zhaoqing.

sentences.zh: 三桂甚惎之，使馬雄如柳州害其家百口。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui hated him bitterly and sent Ma Xiong to Liuzhou to slaughter his entire household of a hundred souls.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui hated him bitterly and sent Ma Xiong to Liuzhou to slaughter his entire household of a hundred souls.

sentences.zh: 弘烈說延齡反正。

translations.literal: Honglie urged Yanling to return to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie urged Yanling to return to loyalty.

sentences.zh: 鎮南將軍覺羅舒恕軍贛州，弘烈密致書言延齡妻孔四貞，定南王有德女，未忘國恩，延齡可招撫。

translations.literal: The Zhennan General Aisin Gioro Shuxu was stationed at Ganzhou; Honglie secretly wrote that Yanling's wife Kong Sizhen, daughter of Prince Dingnan Youde, had not forgotten the state's grace, and Yanling could be won over.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhennan General Aisin Gioro Shuxu was stationed at Ganzhou; Honglie secretly wrote that Yanling's wife Kong Sizhen, daughter of Prince Dingnan Youde, had not forgotten imperial grace and that Yanling could be won over.

sentences.zh: 又致書奉詔招撫督捕理事官麻勒吉，言王師速進南安，弘烈自韶州策應，則兩粵可定。

translations.literal: He also wrote to the imperial commissioner for pacification and bandit suppression Maledji, saying that if the imperial army advanced quickly on Nan'an and Honglie coordinated from Shaozhou, both Guangdong and Guangxi could be secured.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to the imperial commissioner for pacification and bandit suppression Maledji, urging that if the imperial army advanced quickly on Nan'an while Honglie coordinated from Shaozhou, both Guangdong and Guangxi could be secured.

sentences.zh: 舒恕、麻勒吉先後以聞，上嘉其忠誠，授廣西巡撫、徵蠻滅寇將軍，俾增募義兵，便宜行事。

translations.literal: Shuxu and Maledji reported this in succession; the emperor praised his loyalty and appointed him governor of Guangxi and General for Suppressing Barbarians and Exterminating Bandits, with authority to raise volunteer troops and act at discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Shuxu and Maledji reported this in turn; the emperor praised his loyalty and appointed him governor of Guangxi and General for Suppressing Barbarians and Exterminating Bandits, with authority to raise volunteers and act at discretion.

sentences.zh: 弘烈克梧州，下昭平、賀、鬱林、博白、北流、陸川、興業諸州縣，進复潯州，遣平樂知府劉曉齎疏上方略。

translations.literal: Honglie captured Wuzhou, took the prefectures and counties of Zhaoping, He, Yulin, Bobai, Beiliu, Luchuan, and Xingye, advanced to recover Xunzhou, and sent Pingle Prefect Liu Xiao to deliver a memorial setting out strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie captured Wuzhou, took Zhaoping, He, Yulin, Bobai, Beiliu, Luchuan, and Xingye, recovered Xunzhou, and sent Pingle Prefect Liu Xiao to deliver a strategic memorial.

sentences.zh: 論功，加太子少保，並加曉參議道。

translations.literal: When merit was assessed he was made Junior Guardian to the Heir Apparent, and Liu Xiao was also given the rank of vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made Junior Guardian to the Heir Apparent, and Liu Xiao was also given the rank of vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 當是時，馬雄據柳州，三桂諸將分據平樂、南寧、橫州，勢洶洶。

translations.literal: At that time Ma Xiong held Liuzhou, and Wu Sangui's generals held Pingyue, Nanning, and Hengzhou in separate garrisons; the situation was menacing.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ma Xiong held Liuzhou while Wu Sangui's generals occupied Pingyue, Nanning, and Hengzhou; the rebel position looked formidable.

sentences.zh: 弘烈雖屢捷，惟新軍缺砲馬，假於尚之信，弗應。

translations.literal: Although Honglie won repeated victories, his new army lacked artillery and mounts; he borrowed from Shang Zhixin, who did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Although Honglie won repeated victories, his new army lacked artillery and mounts; he asked Shang Zhixin for help, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 吳世琮既殺延齡，陷平樂，襲弘烈梧州，弘烈擊敗之。

translations.literal: After Wu Shizong killed Yanling, seized Pingyue, and attacked Honglie at Wuzhou, Honglie defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Shizong killed Yanling, seized Pingyue, and attacked Honglie at Wuzhou, Honglie repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 十七年，與將軍莽依圖圍平樂，戰失利，弘烈與互訐。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he and General Manggitu besieged Pingyue, were defeated in battle, and Honglie and Manggitu exchanged accusations.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he and General Manggitu besieged Pingyue but were defeated, and Honglie and Manggitu exchanged accusations.

sentences.zh: 詔謂弘烈兵未支俸餉，奮勇收復諸路。

translations.literal: An edict said that Honglie's troops had received no pay or rations yet had fought bravely to recover many routes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict noted that Honglie's troops had received no pay or rations yet had fought bravely to recover many routes.

sentences.zh: 莽依圖自平樂退賀縣，又言糧乏，再退梧州，使弘烈所复郡縣盡棄於賊，因飭莽依圖圖效。

translations.literal: Manggitu withdrew from Pingyue to Hexian, then citing lack of grain withdrew again to Wuzhou, causing all the prefectures and counties Honglie had recovered to be abandoned to the rebels; he was therefore ordered to prove himself.
translations.idiomatic: Manggitu withdrew from Pingyue to Hexian, then citing lack of supplies withdrew again to Wuzhou, leaving all the prefectures and counties Honglie had recovered to the rebels; Manggitu was therefore ordered to prove himself.

sentences.zh: 弘烈督兵進，賊數万渡左江，弘烈戰敗。

translations.literal: Honglie led his troops forward; tens of thousands of rebels crossed the Zuo River, and Honglie was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie led his troops forward, but tens of thousands of rebels crossed the Zuo River and he was defeated.

sentences.zh: 賊陷藤縣，逼梧州。

translations.literal: The rebels seized Teng County and pressed on Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels took Teng County and threatened Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十八年，之信軍至，弘烈分兵水陸，乘賊攻城時三面夾擊，賊潰​​走，遂下藤縣，克平樂，進复桂林。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Zhixin's army arrived; Honglie divided his forces by land and water, and while the rebels were besieging the city struck them from three sides; the rebels broke and fled; he then took Teng County, captured Pingyue, and advanced to recover Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Zhixin's army arrived; Honglie split his forces by land and water and, as the rebels besieged the city, struck them from three sides; the rebels broke and fled; he retook Teng County, captured Pingyue, and recovered Guilin.

sentences.zh: 弘烈密疏言延齡舊部宜善為解散，又言之信怙惡反覆，當早為之所。

translations.literal: Honglie secretly memorialized that Yanling's old troops should be properly disbanded, and also said that Zhixin was vicious and treacherous and should be dealt with early.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie secretly memorialized that Yanling's old troops should be properly disbanded and warned that Zhixin was vicious and unreliable and should be dealt with early.

sentences.zh: 馬雄死，子承廕仍附三桂，受偽封懷寧公，詭言乞款附，弘烈許之，為疏聞。

translations.literal: When Ma Xiong died, his son Chengyin still adhered to Wu Sangui, received the false title Duke of Huaining, falsely claimed to seek terms and submit, and Honglie agreed and memorialized the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After Ma Xiong died, his son Chengyin still adhered to Wu Sangui, held the false title Duke of Huaining, feigned a desire to surrender, and Honglie agreed and reported this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔授承廕昭義將軍統其眾。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Chengyin Zhaoyi General to command his followers.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Chengyin Zhaoyi General to command his followers.

sentences.zh: 弘烈規取雲、貴。

translations.literal: Honglie planned to take Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie planned to take Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 十九年二月，次柳州，承廕期弘烈會議，弘烈至，承廕以其眾叛，襲破其營，執送貴陽。

translations.literal: In the second month of the nineteenth year he halted at Liuzhou; Chengyin set a date for Honglie to meet in council; when Honglie arrived, Chengyin rebelled with his followers, overran his camp, and sent him captive to Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the nineteenth year he halted at Liuzhou; Chengyin summoned Honglie to a council; when Honglie arrived, Chengyin rebelled with his followers, overran his camp, and sent him captive to Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 世璠誘以偽職，弘烈曰：「爾祖未反時，吾已劾奏，料汝家必為叛逆。

translations.literal: Shihuan tempted him with a false office; Honglie said: "Before your grandfather rebelled I had already memorialized against him—I knew your house would turn traitor.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shihuan tempted him with a false office; Honglie said, "Before your grandfather rebelled I had already memorialized against him—I knew your house would turn traitor.

sentences.zh: 汝敢以此言污我邪？

translations.literal: How dare you try to defile me with such words?
translations.idiomatic: How dare you try to defile me with such words?

sentences.zh: 」世琮百計說之，罵益厲。

translations.literal: " Shizong tried every persuasion; Honglie cursed all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: " Wu Shizong tried every persuasion; Honglie cursed all the more fiercely.

sentences.zh: 十月辛丑，遇害。

translations.literal: On day xinchou of the tenth month he was murdered.
translations.idiomatic: On day xinchou of the tenth month he was murdered.

sentences.zh: 十一月，征南將軍穆佔复貴陽，收遺骸，以死狀聞，贈太子太師、兵部尚書，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the southern expedition general Muzhan recovered Guiyang, gathered his remains, reported his death, and posthumously made him Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent and minister of war, with the posthumous title Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the southern expedition general Muzhan recovered Guiyang, gathered his remains, reported his death, and posthumously made him Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent and Minister of War, with the posthumous name Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，允廣西巡撫郝浴請，建雙忠祠於桂林，祀弘烈及馬雄鎮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, granting Guangxi Governor Hao Yu's request, the Double Loyalty Shrine was built at Guilin to worship Honglie and Ma Xiongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, granting Guangxi Governor Hao Yu's request, the Double Loyalty Shrine was built at Guilin to honor Honglie and Ma Xiongzhen.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：方諸籓盛強，朝廷所置督撫，勢不足以相抗。

translations.literal: Commentary: When the feudatories were at their height, the governors and governors-general appointed by the court lacked sufficient power to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: When the feudatories were at their height, the governors and governors-general appointed by the court lacked sufficient power to resist them.

sentences.zh: 文焜雖與三桂分疆而治，所部貳於三桂久矣。

translations.literal: Although Wenkun and Wu Sangui governed separate territories, Wenkun's subordinates had long leaned toward Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: Although Wenkun and Wu Sangui governed separate territories, Wenkun's subordinates had long leaned toward Wu Sangui.

sentences.zh: 若承謨之於精忠，雄鎮之於延齡，皆同城逼處，惟以身殉，無他術也。

translations.literal: As with Chengmo facing Jingzhong and Xiongzhen facing Yanling—all shared the same city with the rebels cheek by jowl and had no recourse but to give their lives; there was no other way.
translations.idiomatic: As with Chengmo facing Geng Jingzhong and Xiongzhen facing Sun Yanling—all shared the same city with the rebels and had no recourse but martyrdom; there was no other way.

sentences.zh: 弘烈異軍特起，又與莽依圖相失，勢孤，遂困於承廕。

translations.literal: Honglie rose as an independent force, then fell out with Manggitu; isolated, he was finally trapped by Chengyin.
translations.idiomatic: Honglie rose as an independent force, then fell out with Manggitu; isolated, he was finally trapped by Chengyin.

sentences.zh: 要其忠義激烈，作士氣，怵寇心，皆不為徒死者。

translations.literal: In essence their fierce loyalty and righteousness rallied morale, deterred the enemy's heart, and none died in vain.
translations.idiomatic: In essence their fierce loyalty rallied morale, deterred the enemy, and none died in vain.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，烈已！

translations.literal: Alas, how fierce!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how fierce!
